decisions: CSharp fixed-array return/field copies use CopyFixedStorageValue and PrepareStaticArrayBlockResult, then EmitHeapAllocate. That canonical allocator branches on pointer-not-null before memcpy and emits the source-owned allocation_failed trap diagnostic.

Current CSharp normal copy cases2 and injected allocation failures2 pass. Copy-function and store-function selectors are declaration-owned and observed in grammar-validated production LLVM before injection; trap exit and exact diagnostics are unchanged.

SLG emitCopyableFixedArrayValue and the direct entry fixed-field copy visibly call allocation then memcpy without the canonical null guard. First verify current Native normal LLVM and resolve its exact source-copy allocation sites before classifying or changing source.

Expected failure identities are distinct from positive runtime identities. The first authored fault-contract cleanup failure and all its outputs remain preserved; no lifecycle or validator was weakened.

Both Native copy sites fail the unchanged null-guard-before-use requirement after the observer retains declaration and ordinal identity. CSharp was requalified under that observer: normal2/fault2 plus related6 all pass.

Propagate explicit ownerIndex through shared fixed-array/struct-copy helpers and their entry/function/control/box/enum callers. Reuse emitAllocationGuard before memcpy/publication. Direct fixed-field and enum copies retain operand/layout code and invoke the same canonical guard with their existing owner. No owner0 fallback or allocation/ownership change.

Keep the allocator null contract, diagnostic text, selected source operation and expected trap unchanged. Scoped fault injection changes only the selected instruction; regression controls cover equal-size calls across and within functions, missing guards and source/ordinal mismatch.
